newsitem.title: CANADA: Manulife mails out C$460 mln bid for Altamira.
newsitem.headline: Manulife mails out C$460 mln bid for Altamira.

text.p: Canadian insurer Manufacturers Life Insurance Co said on Tuesday that it is distributing an offer to acquire the outstanding shares of Altamira Management Ltd currently held by Almiria Capital Corp, Altamira's management and directors.
Manulife is offering C$32 per share which would value the entire transaction at about C$460 million, Manulife spokesman Donald Guloien said in a telephone interview.
Toronto-based Manulife said it also concluded a definitive agreement to boost its stake in Altamira to 58.5 percent from the 30.5 percent it currently holds.
Manulife is Canada's largest insurance company with nearly C$50 billion in assets. Altamira is the country's biggest no-load mutual fund with about C$6.2 billion in mutual fund assets.

The offer gives Altamira shareholders a menu of options involving cash, common and preferred stock in the firm. Altamira management has agreed to reinvest a significant portion of the cash they receive in Altamira mutual funds, Manulife said in a statement.
Almiria's institutional shareholders are welcome to continue as direct or indirect shareholders, Manulife said.

"This transaction marries Altamira's superior wealth management expertise with the resources and reach of one of the world's leading financial institutions," said Manulife president and chief executive Dominic D'Alessandro.

Altamira Investment Services president Philip Armstrong said the offer ends recent uncertainty and speculation about Altamira's ownership. "The offer gives us a strong and ongoing equity interest, which is critical to success in this business," he said.
The deadline for Manulife's offer is November 25. The transaction is subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.
